parsedVerdict.reasoning: All four files serve one concern: cancelling an order. They pass the request along one path: the controller calls CancelOrderService.execute(dto), which builds new CancelOrderCommand(dto) and sends it on the CommandBus. CancelOrderCommandHandler.execute then loads the order and calls order.cancel(reason). It checks order.isValid and order.brokenRules, saves the order and commits the events. The cancellation rule lives only in the domain call order.cancel(reason). The handler reads the result through the aggregate's own brokenRules API and does not re-check it, so the invariant sits in one place. No file skips the module's abstractions: the service always goes through the command, and the command is built only from CancelOrderDto. CancelOrderCommand copies the fields of CancelOrderDto. That is normal command/DTO mapping, not a duplicated rule. One borderline point: cancel-order.dto.ts declares CancelOrderBodyDto, which is documented as the HTTP transport contract for POST /orders/:id/cancel and uses class-validator. That is a slight presentation concern inside an application module. It is still part of the same use case, and CancelOrderDto builds on it through extends, so it does not break cohesion. Two other points concern layer and dependency direction, which is out of scope: the handler depends on the concrete OrderRepository from infrastructure and throws NotFoundException from @nestjs/common.
